memoryText: He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Psalm 91:1 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Psalm 91:1 is the opening of a song of trust, and a fitting summary of the whole unit. After weeks of reading about the tabernacle, the sacrifices, and the priests, this verse takes the images and puts them into the life of a believer.

“He who dwells.” The verb means to sit, to stay, to make a home. It is not a short visit. The Old Testament tabernacle was a place where God dwelt among his people, and now the believer is invited to dwell in God.

“In the shelter of the Most High.” The word “shelter” means a hiding place or a covering. “Most High” is a title that speaks of God’s supreme power over all things. The one who hides in him hides in the greatest of all places.

“Will abide in the shadow of the Almighty.” A shadow is the place of protection from the heat of the sun. “Almighty” is the name Shaddai, the name by which God was known to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The one who lives in God’s shelter is under the care of the God who keeps his promises.

For the Christian, this verse is fulfilled in Jesus. We are “in Christ.” We dwell in him, and he dwells in us (John 15:4-5). The shelter that the tabernacle pictured has been opened to all who believe.
weekInReview: This week you finished the book of Leviticus. You read the calendar of Israel’s festivals, and the Sabbath year and Jubilee with their promise of liberty. You saw the covenant’s blessings and curses and the promise that God remembers his covenant even in exile. You read the last chapter on vows and the tithe. In the Psalms, you prayed Psalm 50, where God says he wants thanksgiving and not empty sacrifice, Psalm 40, where David speaks of an open ear and a heart that delights in God’s will, and Psalm 91, a song of trust in the shelter of the Most High. The week taught that the festivals point to Christ, that God owns everything, and that the heart behind the sacrifice is what he wants.
reflectionQuestions: Israel’s calendar was filled with feasts that taught the people to remember what God had done. What practices help you remember God’s work in your life?
Hebrews 10 places the words of Psalm 40:6-8 on the lips of Jesus. What does it mean to you that he delighted to do the Father’s will on your behalf?
Psalm 91 describes a life lived in the shelter of the Most High. What is one fear you want to bring into that shelter today? Write a short prayer about it.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he is your shelter and shadow.
Thank him for the festivals and psalms that point to Christ.
